name: Host sentence splitting before the fine-tuned formalizer (long and multi-sentence messages)
registered_by: sentence-split-eval-agent (owner idea of 2026-09-29, relayed by the orchestrator: CPU-only evaluation; no training, no GPU)
frozen_before_results: Written after the segmenter, the merge and the S2 variant were built and chosen on the formalizer-v1 development split only (a 120-row dev pilot: 20 long_message rows and 100 short multi-sentence rows, seed 7) and before any S0/S1/S2 prediction of this experiment touched a sealed suite (formalizer-v1 test, formalizer-ood-v1, formalizer-wild-v1). Earlier formalizer-size-v1 predictions on those suites exist and are used only as a rerun control. Any later change is a recorded deviation.
kind: evaluation-only (CPU inference with an existing checkpoint; no optimizer step, no training data change)
question: Does the small fine-tuned formalizer do better on long and multi-sentence messages when the host splits the message into sentences, formalizes each one separately and merges the circuits, and at what speed cost?
owner_idea: Give the small model the message sentence by sentence so as not to confuse it, then collect the circuits; speed should barely change.
changed_factor: How the message is presented to the formalizer: whole (S0), each sentence alone (S1), each sentence with the previous one (S2), with a host merge for S1/S2. Weights, quantization, runtime, decoding and scoring are identical to formalizer-size-v1. Every model input is an exact substring of the user's message (DS021 model boundary: message text only, no context block).

conditions.S0: the whole message (baseline). Predicted again under the same server and load as S1/S2 so latency is paired; the formalizer-size-v1 predictions are compared as a rerun control (wild 796, OOD rows of the short sample, sample500 overlap).
conditions.S2: each sentence with the previous one prepended as the exact message slice from the previous unit's start to this unit's end (no delimiter: a spot check showed that a parenthesized previous sentence is formalized anyway, so no delimiter makes the model skip it). Two merges of the same calls: S2diff (pair output minus the previous unit's own S1 output, as a multiset of DS016 wire keys; needs S1 calls too) and S2dedupe (pair outputs, identical wires dropped). The preregistered S2 is the one with the higher pooled micro wire F1 on the dev pilot; the other is reported as secondary.
conditions.S2hybrid: EXPLORATORY, not part of the decision rule: S1, except units with an EN/RO anaphora cue use their pair output minus the previous unit's output.
conditions.single_unit_messages: a message with one sentence unit is sent once; S1 and S2 reuse the S0 output (identical input).

segmenter: lib/sentence-split.mjs splitSentences: deterministic EN/RO rules (abbreviations Dr./dl./nr./str./etc., initials, decimals, dates, times, balanced quotes and parentheses, list lines, ellipsis, ?/! kept with their sentence, emoji-only units attached to the previous unit). Tuned on dev only.
merge: lib/sentence-split.mjs mergePrograms: per-unit parse (unparsable blocks dropped and counted); unclear wires dropped when any unit has content, else one unclear (ambiguous > no_request > gibberish; gibberish only when every unit is gibberish); identical wires, identical statements and assumed-equal-to-stated dropped; order stated, assumed, query/constraint, each in message order; ids renumbered s1.., a1.., q, q2.., c, c2..

optional.arm: smollm2-135m fv1-size-a4 merged-best Q8_0, only if time allows

model.runtime: llama.cpp 99d4026b llama-server -ngl 0 -t 8 -tb 8 -np 4 -c 32768 --jinja, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty, own server on port 18851 (8 slots after the dev pilot A: -np 8 -c 65536, 8 rows in parallel); lib/formalizer-endpoint.mjs request (message as the only user turn, temperature 0, top_k 1); max_tokens 6144 whole message, 1024 per unit or pair; 4 rows in parallel, the calls of one row in sequence.

short.selection: non-long rows the segmenter cuts into >= 2 units (1,522 test, 365 OOD); 200 per suite, stratified proportionally by (language, code_switch), predict-endpoint sampleRows seed 42

hypotheses.H1: On the 303 long rows, S1 and S2 raise micro wire F1 over S0 (paired 95% interval above 0). PRIMARY.
hypotheses.H2: On the long rows, S1/S2 raise query-part correctness, rows with wire F1 >= 0.9 and tolerant execution equivalence.
hypotheses.H3: On wild, S1/S2 do not lower accepted match or decision match by more than 2 pp (non-inferiority: lower 95% bound > -2 pp) and raise proposition F1 on messages cut into >= 2 units.
hypotheses.H4: On the 400-row short multi-sentence sample, S1/S2 tolerant execution is non-inferior to S0 (lower 95% bound > -2 pp).
hypotheses.H5: Speed barely changes (owner expectation): S1 total model time per message <= 1.25x S0 (ratio of summed per-message latency).
hypotheses.H6: S2 >= S1 on wire F1 (cross-sentence references are resolved).

metrics.per_condition: tolerant execution equivalence (eval/run.mjs evaluate; test/OOD rows), DS016 micro wire F1 / precision / recall (eval/metrics.mjs rowWireComparison over primary and accepted golds), rows with wire F1 >= 0.9, query-part correctness, statement F1; wild: accepted match, decision match, proposition F1 (tools/eval/wild-suite.mjs scoreAgainstAccepted); latency per message = sum of the calls the condition needs (S2diff counts the S1 calls it subtracts), calls per message; merge statistics
metrics.slices: language (en/ro/mixed); short: suite; wild: 1 unit vs >= 2 units, gold with >= 2 statements
metrics.uncertainty: paired cluster bootstrap of metric differences (clusters split_group_id on test/OOD, row on wild; 2,000 resamples, mulberry32 seed 42)
metrics.error_analysis: rows where S1 or S2 is worse than S0 (execution or accepted match lost, or row wire F1 down >= 0.2), heuristically labelled: pronoun left unresolved, question spanning sentences, conditional split, supposition lost, context/question frame, unclear handling, extra/missing wires; examples kept

decision_rule: Recommend host splitting with variant V (S1 or the preregistered S2) if (a) the long-row wire F1 delta V-S0 has a 95% interval above 0, (b) short-sample tolerant execution and wild accepted match are non-inferior (lower bound > -2 pp), and (c) total latency <= 1.5x S0 on long rows. If (a) holds but (b) fails, recommend splitting only for long messages (> 300 characters or >= 4 units, the long-row definition), and report it as a routing rule. Between S1 and S2 prefer the one with higher long wire F1 if the S2-S1 interval excludes 0, else the cheaper S1. Otherwise do not adopt.
limitations_declared: Long-row golds are large (median 27 wires); tolerant execution on long rows is near 0 for every condition by construction, so wire F1 is the primary endpoint.
The formalizer was trained on whole messages; sentence units are a distribution shift of their own (short, sometimes context-free sentences).
Latency is measured with 4 parallel slots on 8 shared threads while other agents' llama-servers run; ratios are paired but absolute numbers are load-dependent.
Single seed, greedy decoding, experiment-grade, no human review; the error-analysis labels are heuristic.

budget.priority_if_short: 360M: long, then wild, then short; 135M only afterwards

dev_pilot_outcome.pilot_a: first run with an earlier segmenter at 4 slots: S0/S1/S2dedupe/S2diff tolerant exec 90.8/46.7/71.7/71.7%, wire F1 0.946/0.907/0.889/0.838; led to two dev-only segmenter fixes (colon lead-ins joined with the next sentence; month abbreviations before a year do not cut)
dev_pilot_outcome.selected_S2: S2dedupe (pooled wire F1 0.892 > S2diff 0.842; same execution)
dev_pilot_outcome.delimiter_check: '(previous sentence) current sentence' on a two-sentence example: the model formalized both sentences, so no delimiter makes it skip the previous sentence; plain message slices are used.
dev_pilot_outcome.note: On in-distribution dev rows splitting already hurts (S1 -47 pp execution): a sentence with a pronoun or ellipsis alone gets an invented referent. The sealed evaluation is run as preregistered anyway.

deviations.what: The 8-slot server restart failed to bind the port, so dev pilot B and 739 wild rows ran on the original 4-slot CPU server; that server was stopped at about 11:57Z by another agent (coordinator notice), and 57 wild rows plus every short/long call after it errored. Errored records were quarantined (work/smollm2-360m/invalid/) and those rows re-run on a new own 8-slot CPU server.
deviations.effect: device and slot count recorded per row; no errored call is scored

deviations.what: Owner instruction to use the GPU for bulk evaluation: starting a GPU llama-server was refused by this session's permission guard (a training job holds the GPU); evaluation stayed on CPU.

Sequential stopping added on the owner's instruction: nested stratified stages (100 rows first). Short sample stopped at stage 100: S1 clearly harmful (-33 pp execution), S2 gain futile (upper bound about +1 pp). Wild had already run in full.
deviations.why: owner rule: stop early when the answer is clear

deviations.what: Experiment stopped early by the orchestrator: superseded by the owner's clause-decomposition language change (compound sentences split into linked clause wires inside the model output); the targets used here are being retired. Long set stopped at 79/303 rows (stage 100 incomplete).
deviations.effect: interim results only; no preregistered decision reached on H1
